location_note: I work remotely across U.S. time zones and I am ready to travel when a customer needs me on site.
headline: Customer-facing engineer for developer platforms and AI infrastructure.
why_looking: I am looking for the next role where I can sit with customers, learn how they want to run a platform, and help them get from a first proof to something they will actually operate. I like work that mixes technical depth with clear writing and a little showmanship.
cover_close: Thank you for your time. I would welcome a conversation.
proud_project: The project I am proudest of is HarborCLI, an open source toolkit I built to stand up a private inference stack on a developer's laptop and then promote the same config into a shared environment. It turned a weekend of yak shaving into a path a teammate could follow in an afternoon.
ai_use: I use AI the way I use a sharp junior teammate: it drafts, it searches, and it reminds me of the boring parts, but I read every line before it goes to a customer or into a repository. I also build small agents with written rules and a human approval step, so the model never sends or merges on its own.
shipped: I have written and shipped production software for internal platforms and open source tools, including APIs, CLI installers, and a small web app that a customer team still uses to track their own rollouts.
llm_agents: I have built and run LLM-based agents with tool use, memory, and a human approval gate. The useful part is not the demo. It is the written rules, the logs, and the moment a person still has to say yes.
open_source: I maintain HarborCLI and I contribute docs and examples to the tools I use in the field. Open source is how I learn a product well enough to teach it.
teaching: I like teaching developers with short field guides and working labs, not slide decks. If I cannot run the path myself, I do not publish it.
client_facing: Most of my week is customer-facing: discovery calls, architecture reviews, proofs of concept, and the awkward middle where a demo has to become an environment someone will keep.
remote: I have worked remotely with customers and teammates across U.S. time zones. I keep written notes, I show up on time, and I write the recap so nobody has to reconstruct the meeting from memory.
additional: I am authorized to work in the United States and I can start on a normal notice period.

proofs.harborcli: I designed and shipped HarborCLI, a small open source toolkit that stands up a private inference stack and then promotes the same config into a shared environment. It is the cleanest example I have of turning a hard platform problem into something a teammate can actually run.
proofs.field_guide: I write field guides and hands-on labs for developer platforms. The format is always the same: a real path, a working example, and the sharp edges written down so the next person does not have to find them the hard way.
proofs.customer_poc: At Northwind Edge I led customer proofs of concept for a platform rollout, from the first architecture sketch to a running environment the account team could hand to operations. The win was not the slide. It was the moment the customer could run it without me.
proofs.agents: I run a small internal agent with written rules, memory, and a human approval step. It drafts and files work, and a person still has to say yes before anything leaves the building.
proofs.teaching: I have given workshops and office hours for customer engineers and developers adopting a new platform, and I measure success by whether they can repeat the path the next week without me.

company_hooks.Acme Cloud: Acme Cloud is building the kind of developer platform I already want to spend my days on: paved paths, honest defaults, and a product that gets out of the way once a team is running.
company_hooks.Globex AI: Globex AI sits at the uncomfortable intersection of inference and real customers, which is exactly the work I like: making a model useful in someone else's environment, not only in a demo.
company_hooks.Northwind Edge: I already know Northwind Edge from the customer side of a platform rollout, and I want to be on the team that helps the next account get there faster.
company_hooks.Initech Platform: Initech Platform is a developer experience product, and I care about that craft: docs, labs, and the last mile that turns a feature into a habit.
company_hooks.Umbrella DevTools: Umbrella DevTools is the kind of toolchain I would actually use, and a customer engineer seat is a chance to bring that into real teams.
company_hooks.Stark Observability: Stark Observability is how teams see what they just shipped, and I have spent enough nights in logs to care about making that path kinder.

role_hooks.se: A solutions engineer seat is the work I already do: discover, design, prove, and then stay close until the customer can run it.
role_hooks.sa: A solutions architect seat lets me go deep on the design and still stay in the room with the customer who has to live with it.
role_hooks.fde: A forward deployed or field engineer role puts me inside the customer's environment, which is where the real constraints show up.
role_hooks.devrel: A developer relations role is teaching with working examples, not slogans, and that is the writing and lab work I already enjoy.
role_hooks.ce: A customer engineer role is hands-on enablement, and I like the mix of technical depth and clear explanation.
role_hooks.default: This is customer-facing platform work, and that is the shape of role I want.

product_use.Acme Cloud: I have used Acme Cloud in labs and personal projects to stand up preview environments, and I like how quickly a new service becomes something you can show a teammate.
product_use.Stark Observability: I have used Stark-style observability stacks to trace a slow request across services, and I would not invent deeper production credentials than I have.
